intent: session capture: address Codex findings on multi-session commit
notes: **CODEX FINDING #1 (critical) — multi-session fix hadn't reached Enterprise-provisioned repos.** My prior commit `df71e8e` updated `.gator/.includes/scripts/{precommit_session.py, gator-session-start.py}` and their `src/gator_command/templates/gator-starter/scripts/` templates, but I MISSED a third copy at `enterprise/enterprise-cli/gator_enterprise_cli/bundled_scripts/`. That's what `repo_init.py::_install_bundled_scripts()` copies into every Enterprise-provisioned repo's `.gator/scripts/`. Result: my sandbox and every future Enterprise install continued to run OLD v1-only single-session code. My earlier "end-to-end verified" claim was only for the monorepo's own hooks — the exact Enterprise bring-up path we care about was still broken. Fix: synced all three copies of both files (byte-identical); added `tests/test_multi_session.py::TestByteIdentityAcrossThreeCopies` parametrized regression pin that will catch any future divergence at test time; updated `scripts-cross-cutting.md` TRIPWIRE to name all three locations explicitly (was originally documented as two-way sync).

**CODEX FINDING #2 — PID recycling protection captured but never used.** The writer recorded `owner_pid_started_at` and the commit message CLAIMED attribution matched both PID and start time, but the picker at `_pick_session_for_commit` only compared raw `owner_pid` membership in the ancestor set. Windows especially recycles PIDs aggressively; a session recording `owner_pid=1234` could later be misattributed to a completely different process that happened to reuse PID 1234. Fix: `_walk_parent_pids()` now returns `[(pid, started_at_or_none), ...]` tuples (Windows PowerShell `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` fetches ProcessId + ParentProcessId + CreationDate in a single call — no extra hop cost; Unix `ps -o ppid=,lstart=` fetches both fields in one call). Picker matches on BOTH pid AND `owner_pid_started_at` via new `_pid_start_times_match()` helper — fuzzy string compare with graceful degradation when either side is None (better to over-attribute than under-attribute on this best-effort check). Regression pins: `test_pid_number_matches_but_started_at_differs_recycled`, `test_pid_match_when_started_at_unavailable_degrades_gracefully`, `test_pid_start_times_match_helper`.

**CODEX FINDING #3 — cross-repo env-override lost vendor identity.** My prior synthesizer set `vendor: "unknown"` when the env-var-referenced session id wasn't in the local file. `render_snippet_json`'s vendor overlay then took `vendor_session["vendor"]` as authoritative — result: snippets had `vendor_inferred: "unknown"` and `session_group_key: "unknown:<id>"` exactly in the cross-repo case the env override was designed to enable first-class. Fix has two parts: (a) new `GATOR_TRANSCRIPT_VENDOR` companion env var — orchestrator can set both id + vendor for full-fidelity cross-repo attribution; (b) when `GATOR_TRANSCRIPT_VENDOR` is unset, the synthesized entry now has `vendor: None` (not "unknown"), and `render_snippet_json` preserves the agent-inferred vendor rather than clobbering with "unknown". `session_group_key` fallback also fixed: explicit vendor → agent-inferred → "unknown" (was `explicit or "unknown"` before, skipping the agent-inferred tier). Regression pins: `test_env_var_vendor_override_sets_synthesized_vendor`, `test_env_var_id_alone_leaves_vendor_none_not_unknown`, `TestRenderSnippetVendorFallback` (2 tests — synthesized vendor=None keeps agent-inferred; explicit vendor in session still overrides).

**10 new tests** on top of the previous commit's 24. Total 34 in `tests/test_multi_session.py`; all pass. Covers all three Codex findings' fix paths AND their previously-broken-state characterization tests (so a future revert of any fix immediately red-flags via the test suite). Byte-identity test is parametrized across both filenames (`precommit_session.py`, `gator-session-start.py`) — will fail loudly if any of the three copies drift.

**Sync verified**: `.gator/.includes/scripts/{precommit_session.py, gator-session-start.py}` == `src/gator_command/templates/gator-starter/scripts/{...}` == `enterprise/enterprise-cli/gator_enterprise_cli/bundled_scripts/{...}` (all three byte-identical via `diff` check post-sync; parametrized test asserts this at test-run time).

**Charter TRIPWIRE updated** in `.gator/charters/scripts-cross-cutting.md::Multi-Session Vendor Attribution`. New sections: three-way sync obligation naming all three locations; PID recycling protection contract; cross-repo vendor identity contract. Each names its regression pin. Prior text (from `df71e8e`) said two-way sync — that under-specification was itself a contributor to Finding #1.

**Live verification will happen on THIS commit**: my current Claude session has a v1 file. The post-commit hook (running the newly-fixed code) should read v1, wrap list-of-one, single-entry short-circuit, and emit snippet with correct transcript_session_id + agent-inferred vendor.
